title: NorthBridge POC - throughput sprint sync
summary: Weekly pilot sync to review throughput numbers from last 48h, tune continuous batching parameters, set concurrency targets and queue/timeout policies. Decided to run two benchmark passes with updated batch windows and to adjust target concurrency per route. Action items assigned and pricing/benchmark spreadsheet to be shared.
next_steps: Redwood to share updated qps/latency workbook and raw logs link
Customer to run the two planned benchmark passes (small/large payload) and return results by next Tuesday
Schedule follow-up with infra SREs to review queueing behavior under burst traffic
action_items: Samira: send qps+latency workbook and link to logs by 2026-03-29
Ethan: push config with batch_window=12ms and max_batch_tokens=2048 to staging by 2026-03-28
Andre: run the small-payload benchmark (50 RPS ramp) and upload results by 2026-03-31
Sofia: validate client-side retry/backoff behavior and share traces by 2026-03-31
transcript:
[14:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll kick off in a min. um, quick roll call?
[14:01] Liam: Liam here.
[14:01] Sofia: Sofia, hi.
[14:01] Andre: Andre on SRE.
[14:01] Priya: Priya in ML.
[14:01] Ethan: Ethan from Redwood engineering.
[14:02] Samira: quick agenda: review last 48 hours of pilot runs, tweak continuous batching and concurrency targets, and agree next steps.
[14:03] Ethan: yep, I pulled the logs and the staging run artifacts. two things stood out: batch formation latency dropped when we lowered the batch_window from 20ms to 12ms, but headroom decreased for tail-latency at peak QPS.
[14:04] Priya: can you clarify — is 12ms the kernel batching timer? we saw some missed KV cache hits during the peak window that correlated with slightly higher token latency.
[14:04] Ethan: right, it's the batch window in the runtime that dictates how long we wait to assemble a batch. with a shorter window we get smaller batches, lower median latency, but we can lose batching efficiency — so throughput per GPU dips a bit.
[14:05] Andre: our concern is steady bursts — we hit 350 RPS for about 45s and queue starts to pile up, we saw more 5xx timeouts on the client side.
[14:05] Samira: are those 5xx from Redwood or from your gateway?
[14:06] Andre: a mix; about 60% were 429s from client-side rate limiter, rest were upstream 504s.
[14:06] Ethan: we traced the 504s to service worker exhaustion on the instance when concurrency spiked over the configured limit. the runtime did backpressure but the client retry pattern amplified the effective load.
[14:07] Sofia: so we should probably tune concurrent request targets per route and set queueing thresholds not just globally.
[14:07] Samira: agree. proposal: set concurrency goal 40 for short-form summarization route and 16 for long-context documents, with adaptive queueing that drops requests after a 2s queue wait and returns suggestive fallback text.
[14:08] Priya: fallback text — is that the structured partial response with best-effort tokens?
[14:08] Ethan: yes, like a graceful degradation: if the request waits >2s we return an outline or compressed answer and enqueue a full async generation if customer wants callback. reduces client perceived failure.
[14:09] Liam: that pattern could work for our user flows. question: what's the expected throughput change if we go to the 12ms batch window and those concurrency targets?
[14:09] Ethan: in our lab the throughput per GPU dropped roughly 8-12% for the long route but median latency improved 15-20ms. For the short route throughput dipped only ~5% but p50 latency improved significantly.
[14:10] Samira: we recommended two benchmark passes: small payload (short route) at stepped RPS up to 300, and large payload (long route) to 120 RPS. run with new batch_window and the concurrency targets. compare to baseline logs attached in the workbook.
[14:10] Andre: any guidance on client retry/backoff? we saw tight loops that re-tried immediately.
[14:11] Ethan: please use exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries; avoid immediate synchronous retries. also respect 429 Retry-After if present. we'll include sample middleware snippet in the workbook.
[14:12] Sofia: what's the KV cache hit rate impact? Priya noted misses during burst windows.
[14:12] Priya: yes, hit rate went from ~82% down to 68% during spikes, likely due to fragmented request patterns and tokenization differences.
[14:13] Ethan: we can increase KV cache warmup and pin common prefixes in the cache for the pilot — config toggle on the runtime. that should raise hit rate back into the 80s.
[14:13] Liam: are there any risks to enabling aggressive pinning? does it increase memory pressure?
[14:14] Ethan: modestly, yes — but for the pilot's GPU profile we have slack. we can monitor mem usage and roll back if it hits threshold.
[14:14] Samira: also wanted to mention fallback routing: we have a compatible quantized variant that we can route to when load is >85% for cost/perf tradeoff. it's slightly lower quality on nuanced queries.
[14:15] Priya: could we A/B a small percent to measure quality delta?
[14:15] Ethan: absolutely — can do a 5% canary to the quantized variant for 24 hours and measure eval metrics on a holdout prompt set.
[14:16] Andre: for the queueing policy, can Redwood provide recommended thresholds and the translation to our gateway settings?
[14:16] Samira: yes, we'll include recommended queue_depth thresholds per route plus suggested Retry-After semantics.
[14:17] Sofia: timeline — if we push the config to staging Thursday, run the small benchmark Friday, and the large Monday, we can converge next Tuesday.
[14:17] Samira: that matches our ask. Ethan, will you push the change?
[14:18] Ethan: I'll push batch_window=12ms, max_batch_tokens=2048, enable KV pinning for prefixes, and set initial concurrency targets. I'll also add instrumentation hooks for queue wait time and per-batch sizes.
[14:18] Liam: perfect. also — pricing question briefly: if throughput efficiency drops with smaller batches, how will that affect pilot cost estimates?
[14:19] Samira: we'll update the workbook to show delta per 10% throughput loss and present cost sensitivity for both hosted and dedicated scenarios.
[14:19] Priya: any impact on token accounting or is it purely compute?
[14:19] Ethan: token accounting stays the same; it's GPU utilization causing cost delta. we'll show cost per effective token served in the spreadsheet.
[14:20] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[14:21] Samira: wrap-up: run two benchmarks, update workbook, push config, client retry changes, and follow up with SRE deep dive. next sync same time next week unless we need an interim checkpoint.
[14:22] Liam: sounds good, thanks all.
[14:22] Sofia: thanks!
[14:22] Andre: thanks.
[14:23] Samira: meeting adjourned.
notes: Attached: qps-latency-workbook.xlsx (shared link in chat), sample retry middleware, staging logs link. Customer to do two benchmark runs; Redwood to provide config and recommended thresholds.
